articles.title: Former Brighton and Port Vale captain Doug Loft dies at 39 as tributes pour in from 9 heartbroken clubs
articles.summary: Former Port Vale and Gillingham captain Doug Loft has tragically died at 39, leading to heartfelt tributes from clubs he played for. Remembering a true leader and inspirational figure on and off the pitch.
articles.body: Doug Loft, the former Port Vale and Gillingham captain who spent more than a decade playing across English football, has died at the age of 39 following a medical emergency over the weekend. Tributes have poured in from the clubs he represented, with Port Vale remembering a leader whose commitment helped secure promotion and former manager Micky Adams recalling the pride Loft took in captaining the team.Loft made his mark at Port Vale after emerging at BrightonLoft began his senior career at non-League Hastings United before joining Brighton & Hove Albion in January 2006, shortly after his 20th birthday. He made 49 appearances for Brighton before moving to Port Vale in the summer of 2009, beginning a five-season spell that would become the defining chapter of his career.The versatile midfielder made 196 appearances for Port Vale, scoring 19 goals, and quickly became a favourite among supporters through his work rate and determination. He was named the club's Player of the Season for 2011-12 before being appointed captain ahead of the following campaign, when Vale secured promotion from League Two under Adams.Loft left Vale Park in 2014 to join Gillingham, where he continued his leadership role and made 70 appearances during two seasons in League One. His professional career also included spells at Colchester United, Shrewsbury Town and Dagenham & Redbridge, before he continued playing in non-League football with Billericay Town, Margate and Tonbridge Angels.He eventually retired from playing in 2023, having represented clubs across different levels of the English game.Port Vale and former manager Micky Adams lead tributesPort Vale confirmed Loft's death in a statement, remembering the former captain for his contribution to the club during five seasons in Burslem.“He will be remembered fondly by everyone at the club, not only for his achievements on the pitch but for the commitment and leadership he showed throughout his time in Burslem,” the club said.Vale added: “The thoughts and heartfelt condolences of everyone at Port Vale are with Doug’s family, friends, former team-mates and all those who knew him, at this incredibly sad time.”The club also confirmed that, with the family's blessing, it had requested permission from the English Football League for players to wear black armbands and observe a minute's silence before the upcoming match against Chesterfield.Speaking to the BBC, former manager Adams paid tribute to Loft's pride in representing Vale, recalling a player who took his responsibilities as captain seriously.“There was nobody more proud to be captain of the Vale,” Adams said.BBC Radio Stoke's Phil Bowers also recalled Loft's leadership during his five years at the club, noting that he captained the side during its promotion-winning 2012-13 campaign. Adams said Loft had led with “enthusiasm and endeavour”, while Bowers reported that he left in 2014 to move back south with his family.Brighton, Gillingham and Tonbridge Angels pay tributeBrighton expressed their sadness following news of Loft's death, remembering a player who had represented the Seagulls before establishing himself at Port Vale.“Everyone at the Albion is devastated to hear the news of Doug Loft’s sudden passing at the age of 39,” the club wrote on social media. “Doug played 42 times for the club & will always be fondly remembered by fans & staff alike.”Gillingham, where Loft also served as captain, confirmed that the former midfielder had died following a medical emergency over the weekend.“The Football Club is absolutely devastated to announce the death of former Gills Captain, Doug Loft,” the club said. “Our thoughts and condolences are with Doug’s wife Laura, their children Freya and Amelie, along with his friends and family at this very difficult time.”Tonbridge Angels also paid tribute to Loft, describing him as “a true professional, a talented player and a wonderful person”, while sending their condolences to his wife, children and wider family.Billericay Town extended their “prayers, sincere condolences and sympathy” to Loft's loved ones, and Dagenham & Redbridge said they were “deeply saddened” by the passing of their former player.Loft is survived by his wife, Laura, and their two daughters, Freya and Amelie. articles.title: Agoumé, sobre la expulsión de Isaac: "No creo que haya hecho nada malo"
articles.standfirst: El francés no entendió que Cordero Vega mostrara la segunda tarjeta amarilla al delantero del Sevilla
articles.summary: El francés no entendió que Cordero Vega mostrara la segunda tarjeta amarilla al delantero del Sevilla
articles.body: El Sevilla cosechó su segundo empate a domicilio de la temporada, esta vez ante el Levante. Los blanquirrojos lograron una ventaja de dos goles con las dianas de Robbie Ure y Félix Correia y los granotas respondieron con los tantos de Iván Romero y Adrián Dela. En el minuto 95, Isaac Romero volvió a adelantar a los visitantes y mandó a callar a la grada; el colegiado Adrián Cordero Vega decidió entonces sancionar al delantero con su segunda tarjeta amarilla, dejando a los suyos en inferioridad numérica antes del último gol marcado por Ifeanyi Ndukwe (3-3). Lucien Agoumé reconoció tras el choque no haber entendido la expulsión de Isaac. "El problema es que el árbitro nos expulsa a un jugador por una celebración. Eso nunca lo había visto antes. No creo que Isaac haya hecho nada malo. Estaba celebrando su gol como lo hace siempre, pero hoy el árbitro ha decidido castigarlo. Después, el Levante nos estaba atacando mucho en los últimos minutos y hemos encajado ese gol. Entonces, espero la explicación del árbitro sobre esta tarjeta roja", explicó el centrocampista francés en los micrófonos de Movistar LaLiga. A pesar de la expulsión, Agoumé quiso hacer autocrítica por la cantidad de ocasiones desperdiciadas por su equipo: "Son dos puntos perdidos hoy por cómo ha ido el partido porque nos ponemos dos goles arriba. No podemos encajar un gol tan rápido después de haber metido el segundo. Y la verdad que en la segunda parte hemos fallado mucho, demasiado errores en Primera División como para ganar un partido". Con el empate en el Ciutat de València, el Sevilla se marcha hasta los 14 puntos de 24 posibles, continuando con su buen inicio de campaña. "Nosotros creemos en nuestro grupo, creemos en nuestro equipo. Cada partido lo vamos a competir y es lo que estamos haciendo hasta ahora. Después, los puntos nos los hemos ganado dentro del campo y lo que la gente de fuera puede pensar de nosotros no nos importa mucho", concluyó Agoumé.

articles.title: Torcedor cria fábrica de bandeirões e fatura R$ 40 mil por mês | G1
articles.standfirst: Morador de Diadema (SP), Rogério Maldonado transformou uma bandeira produzida para a própria torcida em uma empresa especializada em bandeirões para estádios.
articles.summary: Morador de Diadema (SP), Rogério Maldonado transformou uma bandeira produzida para a própria torcida em uma empresa especializada em bandeirões para estádios.
articles.body:
Para muitas torcidas, o bandeirão é mais do que um adereço de arquibancada . É símbolo de identidade, pertencimento e apoio ao time.

Foi justamente a partir dessa paixão que o empreendedor Rogério Maldonado, conhecido como Bambu, construiu um negócio especializado na fabricação de bandeiras gigantes para estádios .

Em Diadema , na Grande São Paulo, ele comanda uma empresa que hoje produz peças para clubes, federações, patrocinadores e eventos corporativos.

"É a bandeira que representa a torcida no estádio, é o estandarte. Quando o time entra em campo daquele bandeirão, abre uma coisa que deslumbra, que mexe com os sentimentos dos torcedores e dos jogadores também", afirma o empreendedor.

A trajetória começou de forma improvisada. Torcedor apaixonado, Rogério nunca havia confeccionado uma bandeira quando surgiu a necessidade de produzir uma para sua própria organizada. Com experiência em maquiagem artística e trabalho manual, decidiu encarar o desafio.

Torcedor cria fábrica de bandeirões e fatura R$ 40 mil por mês — Foto: Reprodução/PEGN

"Quando a minha torcida precisou de uma bandeira de imediato, eu falei: 'eu vou pintar'. Já tinha técnica de pincel e conhecimentos de arte final. Comprei o pano, desenhei e pintei a bandeira para a torcida", relembra.

O trabalho chamou atenção e logo veio uma encomenda inesperada: um cliente da Califórnia, nos Estados Unidos, procurou Rogério para fazer uma bandeira. Depois de concluir o projeto, ele publicou o resultado nas redes sociais e percebeu que havia demanda para o serviço.

"Eu postei no Instagram a bandeira que tinha feito para a Califórnia. Aí os amigos começaram a perguntar: 'você está fazendo bandeira agora também?'. Foi ali que eu descobri que dava para fazer disso um negócio", conta.

No início, ele era responsável por todas as etapas da produção. Comprava os tecidos, acompanhava a costura, fazia as entregas e administrava os pedidos. O crescimento da empresa começou quando clientes corporativos passaram a exigir nota fiscal.

"Uma empresa me procurou e disse que precisava de nota fiscal. Foi quando abri um MEI para atender essa demanda. Depois, a empresa foi crescendo", diz.

Hoje, a operação atende grandes clubes do futebol brasileiro e entidades ligadas ao esporte. O negócio recebeu investimento de cerca de R$ 80 mil para ampliar a estrutura produtiva e registra faturamento médio mensal de R$ 40 mil.

Entre os projetos mais marcantes está a produção de um bandeirão para o Fluminense com 220 metros de comprimento e 90 metros de altura , utilizado em uma semifinal no Maracanã.

"A maior bandeira conjunta que fizemos teve quase 21 mil metros quadrados e fechou o setor sul inteiro do Maracanã", afirma Rogério.

Outro trabalho de destaque foi a produção de diversas bandeiras para revestir todos os setores do Morumbi durante uma celebração do aniversário do São Paulo Futebol Clube.

Mas o mercado foi além dos estádios. Atualmente, a empresa também produz materiais em tecido para eventos corporativos, campanhas promocionais e empresas.

"Hoje fazemos tudo o que você pensar em impressão em tecido. Além de bandeirões, faixas, mosaicos e camisões para arquibancada, também atendemos empresas com banners e bandeiras institucionais", explica o empresário.

Entre os clientes está Johnny’s Rocha 'Carranca', vice-presidente de uma torcida organizada do Corinthians. Para ele, o valor das bandeiras vai muito além do visual.

"Para nós, da Estopim da Fiel, a bandeira representa uma vida. Representa todo o esforço que a gente faz no nosso dia a dia", afirma.

Segundo Carranca, a dedicação dos torcedores acontece durante toda a semana, não apenas nos dias de partida.

"O jogo não é só no domingo. Para a gente, começa na segunda-feira e vai até o domingo seguinte. Tem logística, reserva de ingresso e preparação. Por isso, ver o bandeirão no estádio representa muito", diz.

A relação construída ao longo dos anos transformou Rogério em uma referência no segmento. "Ele é uma referência para nós quando o assunto é bandeira e faixa. Sempre que a torcida precisa, a gente procura o trabalho dele", afirma o cliente.

Partindo praticamente do zero, com apenas um notebook para criar as artes, o empreendedor viu a paixão pelas arquibancadas se transformar em uma empresa com cerca de 11 colaboradores e planos de expansão.

"Comecei do zero, só com o notebook que eu tinha. Hoje temos quase 11 colaboradores e projetos novos já começando a acontecer. Isso me orgulha muito", afirma Rogério.

articles.title: Texas A&M's Mike Elko Apologizes for Ripping Media Outlet with Viral 'Cesspool' Comment After Loss
articles.summary: Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko apologized Monday after referring to local media outlet TexAgs, which is co-owned by Billy Liucci, as a "cesspool" following Saturday's 27-6 loss to Missouri.
articles.body:
Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko apologized Monday after referring to local media outlet TexAgs, which is co-owned by Billy Liucci, as a "cesspool" following Saturday's 27-6 loss to Missouri.

"I think everybody knows I have a tremendous relationship with Billy," Elko told reporters . "I appreciate Billy. I appreciate him being here today. There's nothing about him and I that have ever been off since 2018. I think everybody knows I appreciate our fanbase and everything that they're about and everything that they mean to Texas A&M. Outside of that, I'll leave it alone.

"I regret the way it was taken. I regret the way it came out. I regret the way it ran. That certainly was never my intention. And certainly, throughout the course of that interview, at no point ever did I lend any blame to anything other than myself. I am the reason why this team is struggling. I have owned that since this has started. I continue to own that. It's my job to figure out how to get it better."

The initial comments included Elko saying, "There's one group that I really don't care much about. Billy's cesspool can go be Billy's cesspool. Our fanbase: Stay with us, be behind us, we're going to build something that we told you we were going to build. We're in a really bad spot right now, but we'll work our way out of it."

That drew a critical response from Liucci:

ESPN's Max Olson noted TexAgs was founded in 1997 and stands as the "largest entity" that covers the Aggies on a daily basis. The independent fan site features a message board but also partners with the school for NIL opportunities.

To say there is frustration surrounding the Texas A&M football program at this point would be an understatement.

The Aggies reached the College Football Playoff last season, which was Elko's second as the head coach, and entered the 2026 campaign at No. 8 in the preseason Associated Press Top 25.

Fans surely expected another run at the CFP, but the team has looked nothing like a realistic contender through six games.

Saturday's loss dropped Texas A&M to 3-3 overall and an ugly 1-3 in SEC play. It also lost to Kentucky and LSU with the latter defeat coming by 29 points. The Aggies failed to score a touchdown in the loss to LSU and the loss to Missouri.

With upcoming games against Alabama, Tennessee, Oklahoma and Texas, things could get even uglier for Elko's club this season, which will only lead to more criticism.

articles.title: Wales v Albania: Players given history lesson before Women's World Cup semi-final second leg
articles.summary: Wales take a 1-0 lead into their play-off semi-final second leg against Albania as they chase a place at next year's tournament in Brazil.
articles.body:
Captain Angharad James has revealed Wales' players have been given a play-off history lesson as they bid to take another step towards a first Women's World Cup.

Wales take a 1-0 lead into their play-off semi-final second leg against Albania in Llanelli on Tuesday as they chase a place at next year's tournament in Brazil.

James has experienced the joy of play-off success and the pain of losing out at this stage of qualifying.

And the 32-year-old says Wales have moved to ensure every member of a squad featuring numerous youngsters is "up to speed" on what is at stake.

"We had a players' meeting on the first day just to integrate the group and to make sure everyone was aware of the importance of this camp and what it means to represent Wales and what it means to be in a play-off position.

"We have to give everything. It's a final game for us and every game is.

"[The meeting was] just to make sure everyone's up to speed."

Women's World Cup qualifying play-off semi-final second leg

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC One Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

Wales have reached the play-off stages of qualification for a major tournament for only the third time in the history of the women's national side.

Their first attempt, in qualifying for the 2023 World Cup, ended in agony.

Gemma Grainger's team beat Bosnia-Herzegovina at the semi-final stage before - despite taking an early lead - losing out to a goal late in extra time of the final in Switzerland.

Two years later, it was an entirely different story as Wales overcame Slovakia and the Republic of Ireland to reach Euro 2025, the first women's major tournament in the nation's history.

Thanks in part to a lengthy injury list, James is one of only five players who began the decisive game in Dublin 22 months ago who are in contention to start against Albania.

The 146-cap Seattle Reign midfielder was also part of the side left heartbroken by that late defeat in Zurich in October 2022.

"[They were] two very different feelings after both games," James said.

"The feeling that we had out in Switzerland, going so close in extra time and narrowly missing out, it fuelled us for Dublin.

"There's a big group of us that experienced that and at the start of this camp we made sure the whole group was aware of how it feels to be on both ends of that."

Gemma Evans is another member of the current Wales squad who featured in those pivotal games against Switzerland and the Republic of Ireland.

The centre-back famously lost a tooth when making a challenge during the Aviva Stadium success - with pictures of that moment featuring in last week's team meeting.

"The highs of that [included] Gemma losing a tooth and unfortunately it made it on to the big screen, we showed the girls that," James said with a smile.

"We've had so many high moments with this group and hopefully we've got the biggest one yet to come with the World Cup."

There is much work to do before Wales can begin planning for a World Cup debut.

After a scruffy performance in Shkoder last Friday, the first task is to get past an Albania side that Wales beat twice during the group phase of this qualifying campaign.

Should they manage that, Wilkinson's team will face a play-off final in early December, probably against a Norway side who are ranked 14th in the world.

Wales would start as underdogs against the Norwegians, who play their second leg at home to Romania on Tuesday evening having won 2-0 away in the first leg.

Even if Wales were to come through a potential Norway final, they may then have to negotiate inter-confederation play-offs next February before a World Cup place is guaranteed.

James, who believes the qualification process should be simplified, says the focus for now is Albania, and on starting from scratch despite Wales' lead from the first leg.

"If we overthink that we have a 1-0 advantage then I don't think it's a good thing as players," she said.

"So we're focusing on it being a new 90-minute game. It's a clean sheet and we're going out there to perform and to win again."

articles.title: Jithin’s stoppage-time strike helps NEUFC sink Mohun Bagan
articles.summary: They could not overcome the heavyweights in pre-season, losing in the semifinals of the Durand Cup and settling for a draw in the IFA Shield group stage.
articles.body: They could not overcome the heavyweights in pre-season, losing in the semifinals of the Durand Cup and settling for a draw in the IFA Shield group stage.However, Juan Pedro Benali's men delivered when it mattered most as NorthEast United FC snatched a dramatic late 1-0 win against Mohun Bagan Super Giant in their Indian Super League opener in Guwahati on Monday.Playing in front of their fans at the Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium, it was super-sub Jithin MS who struck the winner in the first minute of stoppage time after Bagan had dominated much of the 90 minutes with their attacks, while NEUFC relied on the brilliance of Alaaeddine Ajaraie to breach the visitors' defence.The first half produced some enthralling end-to-end action, with Mohun Bagan pressing from the word go and the Highlanders responding with attacks of their own after the opening 10 minutes.It was Lallianzuala Chhangte, in his new green-and-maroon colours, who dominated the early exchanges, having been named in the starting XI by coach Panagiotis Dilmperis ahead of regular Bagan winger Manvir Singh. Soon after, however, fellow new signing Lee Erwin began to grow into the game.The Scot also came closest to breaking the deadlock with a volley that dropped into the goal after hitting the bar, only for the offside flag to deny him. His physicality and pace began to pose all sorts of problems for the NEUFC defence. However, the Highlanders' new signing Nikhil Barla remained up to the task in his defensive role.The combination of Chhangte and Erwin made a Bagan breakthrough look imminent, only for the NEUFC defence, led by skipper Asheer Akhtar, to soak up the pressure every time.At the other end, Highlanders talisman Ajaraie looked threatening with his individual brilliance, while Ethyan Gonzalez's crosses repeatedly found runners inside the box, but each move was thwarted by the blocking and marking of Alberto Rodriguez and Lalengmawia Ralte.It was Rodriguez who came close for the visitors in the 43rd minute when his long-range effort whistled past the top-left corner of the NEUFC goal.While both coaches made a couple of changes after the break, it was the combination of Sahal Abdul Samad and Erwin that created two chances in quick succession in the 54th minute. Erwin first produced a feeble effort from close range after a Sahal pass and then failed to keep down a tricky volley, sending it over the bar.Soon after, Dilmperis replaced Erwin with Miguel Ferreira and brought on regular attackers Liston Colaco and Manvir Singh, along with Kashmiri forward Suhail Ahmed Bhat, in search of the elusive goal.Ajaraie had a couple of good chances in the 72nd and 75th minutes respectively but had Mehtab Singh stand strong with a tackle in the first while his dipping long volley that beat goalkeeper was disallowed by the referee’s whistle.On the other end, an incessant series of attacks from Bagan was met with some frantic but successful defending from the home side as Benali’s men mostly resorted to counter-attacks to find a goal against the run of play.Bhat could have got Bagan a goal towards the end when he failed to connect to a perfect cross from Colaco from the right at goal-mouth in the 87th minute and hit the woodwork a couple of minutes later.However, roared on by their fans, NEUFC began creating chances of their own towards the end of regulation time and, in the 95th minute, the ball fell to Jithin after a Gonzalez piledriver struck the woodwork. articles.title: De Bruyne se reinventa para vestirse de 'king' antes del Villarreal: "En esa posición alargaría su carrera dos años"
articles.standfirst: 'Tintín' se reivindicó con un doblete ante el Frosinone (3-0) jugando cerca del doble pivote
articles.summary: 'Tintín' se reivindicó con un doblete ante el Frosinone (3-0) jugando cerca del doble pivote
articles.body: Kevin de Bruyne (Drongen, 1991) no tuvo el inicio soñado en Nápoles. En una temporada marcada por la falta de continuidad por culpa de las lesiones y la nula sintonía con Antonio Conte, el ex del Manchester City apenas registró cinco goles y cuatro asistencias en 21 partidos (1.360'). 'King Kev', a sus 35 años, parecía más fuera que dentro del reino que encumbró a Diego Armando Maradona. "Estoy contento de que Conte se marche. Si se hubiera quedado, no habría sido lo ideal para mí", aseguraba el internacional belga, que llegó a poner en duda su continuidad: "Todavía me queda un año de contrato, pero quiero hablar de ello. Mucho dependerá de qué tipo de estrategia se elija". Unas declaraciones que hicieron estallar a Giovanni Manna. "De Bruyne no tiene que tomar ninguna decisión. Se unió a este proyecto el año pasado y firmó por dos años más un año opcional. Tuvo un año complicado y ha rendido menos de lo que potencialmente puede dar, pero fue una inversión importante en términos económicos y de imagen", aseguró el director deportivo del Nápoles. Poco a poco, con 'Max' Allegri en el banquillo, De Bruyne vuelve a parecerse a De Bruyne. Marcó y asistió en la victoria sobre el Genoa (0-2) y se reivindicó con un doblete en el triunfo sobre el Frosinone (3-0) justo antes de visitar al Villarreal en Champions. Lo hizo, paradójicamente, jugando más cerca de la base, junto a Lobotka, en el 1-3-4-2-1 que dispuso Allegri. Estrenó su cuenta en el 29', transformando con una calma parsimoniosa el penalti que, previamente, había fallado Rasmus Hojlund y remató la 'faena' en el 94', culminando en boca de gol un 'pase de la muerte' de Giovane. "En mi opinión, es un jugador extraordinario. Bueno, no es mi opinión: simplemente es así. Si empieza a jugar de mediocampista en la base, mejorará aún más. Le dije: podrías alargar tu carrera un par de años si te pones en esa posición, pero no le gusta mucho, prefiere divertirse jugando más adelante, pero jugó un buen partido, como siempre", sugería Massimiliano Allegri. "Siempre he jugado de número 8 o número 10. Esta vez jugué en una posición diferente, pero no hay problema. Me han pedido que juegue en varias posiciones, tenemos muchos partidos y puedo hacerlo", reconocía De Bruyne a 'Sky Sports' tras el partido. Atrás queda su particular 'destierro'. 'Tintín', que suma tres goles y una asistencia, vuelve a sonreír. "Nunca contemplé la idea de dejar el 'Napoli' este verano, no hablé de ello con nadie. Cuando digo algo, soy muy directo, pero a la gente no le gusta y arma un escándalo", asegura. Lo único seguro es que bajo el nuevo 'libreto' se siente más cómodo: "Conte es muy rígido, más centrado en la relación profesional. No hay conexión con los jugadores. Allegri , en cambio, es más relajado, más formal y, por lo que he visto, se preocupa más por el vínculo personal". A pesar del irregular comienzo del Nápoles, octavo a seis puntos de Inter y Lazio, no renuncia a pelear por el 'Scudetto': "Será una carrera muy dura otra vez, aunque creo que el Inter es el favorito".

articles.title: El Cuti Romero, un ‘capitán’ para aspirar a los trofeos
articles.standfirst: Tras cambiar la cara del Atlético ‘fortificando’ la defensa, recibe a un Manchester United al que negó el último título al que se acercó: la Europa League de 2025
articles.summary: Tras cambiar la cara del Atlético ‘fortificando’ la defensa, recibe a un Manchester United al que negó el último título al que se acercó: la Europa League de 2025
articles.body: Pese a que su primera titularidad en Liverpool no se tradujo en una portería a cero, los dos goles encajados por Oblak no ocultaron que el Atlético volvía a tener a un mariscal en la defensa como en los primeros años del Cholismo fue Godín. En números, quedó reflejado en los cuatro partidos siguientes, en los que el esloveno sólo lamentaría el gol de penalti del pasado sábado en Mendizorroza con el Cuti Romero sobre el verde (el tanto del Real Madrid en este periodo se produjo nada más ser sustituido el argentino). En sensaciones, su sola presencia tiene un impacto aún mayor. Bien lo sabe el Manchester United, el rival al que más veces se ha enfrentado pero que sólo ha conseguido vencerle en tres de sus diez enfrentamientos (tres derrotas y cuatro empates), tras ver cómo el Cuti lideraba a un Tottenham herido de muerte en la final de la Europa League de 2025, convirtiéndose en el último capitán en impedir que las vitrinas de Old Trafford se engordaran con un título más. No obstante, no le hace falta portar brazalete alguno en el Atlético (sí lo ha heredado en la selección Argentina de un Messi que siempre lo recomendó para el Barcelona) para justificar en apenas un mes (o quizás desde el primer día que pisó el vestuario y ya mandaba y arengaba incluso sin haber empezado a jugar) el viejo empeño de Simeone de tenerlo en sus filas. O que el técnico aceptara perder a Ruggeri y Molina para hacerle sitio. O que Julián siempre haya sostenido que se trata del central más complicado al que se ha medido. Así que, aunque una temporada y media más tarde lo deseado, por fin el Atlético vuelve a armarse a fortificarse a partir de un central con una jerarquía mundial que permite soñar con pelear por cualquier trofeo. Lo celebra Oblak, lo agradecen unos compañeros a los que mejora y, sobre todo, lo temen los rivales, con Mbappe como uno de los delanteros a los que ya ha dejado a cero). El Cuti sí que es un infierno para los Diablos Rojos.

articles.standfirst: El segundo entrenador del Galatasaray analiza para MARCA en cruce de Champions
articles.summary: El segundo entrenador del Galatasaray analiza para MARCA en cruce de Champions
articles.body: Ismael García (Ourense, 1988) llegó al Galatasaray en 2022 y está viviendo unas temporadas de grandes éxitos. El segundo entrenador del equipo turco analiza para MARCA el encuentro de esta noche contra el Barça. No escatima en elogios hacia el conjunto culé, al que considera, junto al PSG, candidato a ganar la Champions, pero advierte de que su equipo ofrece su mejor versión en casa. Ismael García reconoce que respira más tranquilo con la baja de Raphinha y, en cuanto al Balón de Oro, cree que Lamine Yamal ganará muchos, pero este año su apuesta es Harry Kane. Respuesta. Esta es la quinta temporada que llevo aquí y todo muy bien. Hemos ganado la liga los últimos cuatro años, igualando el mayor registro de la historia, pero ahora queremos lograr la quinta, algo que nunca ha ocurrido en Turquía. R. La verdad es que sí. El año pasado me crucé con el Atlético de Madrid y ahora recibir al Barcelona me hace mucha ilusión. Además, guardo muy buenos recuerdos de mi etapa en la Ciudad Condal, en el Centre d'Esports L'Hospitalet. Fui varias veces al Spotify Camp Nou y no me olvido, por ejemplo, de la remontada contra el PSG. R. No hay duda que nuestra afición siempre nos ayuda. Y no es algo que digo yo, si miras las estadísticas del equipo en Europa verás la diferencia de resultados entre los partidos de casa y los de fuera. Creo que la superioridad real del Barcelona la podemos contrarrestar con nuestra calidad y la presión del estadio. R. Genera mucho respeto. Asustar no porque el fútbol es un juego y durante un encuentro pueden pasar muchas cosas. Para mí, el Barcelona es el equipo que mejor está jugando en este inicio de temporada y encima tiene una plantilla, no un once, muy buena. Sin duda, a día de hoy es el equipo que más me gusta ver. R. Sí, claro. No te voy a decir otra cosa. Hay mucha gente que dice que le gusta que todos los buenos estén en el campo, pero... Es cierto que como amante del fútbol te gusta ver a los mejores, pero, en este caso, si no puede jugar, mejor. R. No tengo ninguna duda. Lo meto en el top-3 de equipos con opciones de ganarla... incluso diría que podría reducir la lista a dos candidatos: PSG y Barça. El Barcelona está ahora en un nivel de madurez increíble. R. Es un proyecto de continuidad y sentido común. Creen en la cantera y, lo más importante, ponen a los jugadores. Hay muchos clubes con grandes canteras, pero hay que atreverse a apostar por esos jugadores. He estado en muchos países, pero en España tenemos una cantera de élite mundial. Espart tiene una gran calidad, pero a mi me enamora el juego de Marc Bernal. R. Estamos hablando de un plantilla con muy buenos jugadores, algunos veteranos y mucha juventud. Estos años que lleva Flick han permitido al equipo aprender mucho. Por ejemplo, cuando fue eliminado de la Champions contra el Inter. Creo que hay muchos jugadores que están, como se dice en inglés, en su prime. Tiene un gran presente y futuro. R. A corto plazo, sin duda, el partido contra el Barcelona. Queremos dejar muy buenas sensaciones, eso sería bueno para nosotros y para todo el fútbol turco. Creo que hemos vuelto a hacer una muy buena plantilla este verano, pero ahora no nos marcamos un objetivo: octavos, cuartos... ya veremos. R. Sí. Salvando las distancias, porque ya hemos dicho que el Barcelona tiene calidad para ganar la Champions, nos asemejamos un poco en ese querer dominar el partido. En la posesión, el rey es el Barça pero nosotros tenemos también esa agresividad post pérdida y llevamos la línea defensiva alta. R. Es que esto es la Champions y, en esta competición, están los mejores jugadores. Seguro que se verá un buen partido. R. Sí me sorprendió un poco porque, aunque estaba destinado a ir a un grande si volvía a España, parecía que el Barça ya tenía esa posición más o menos bien cubierta. Pero, claro, cuando hablamos de Rodri, hablamos de uno de los tres mejores centrocampistas del mundo y, además, aporta una gran madurez y liderazgo. R. Lamine Yamal ganará muchos en su carrera, pero este año creo que será para Harry Kane.

articles.title: Yorke: "No veo posible que el United gane la Champions ahora"
articles.standfirst: La leyenda del United analiza en MARCA la vuelta de los Red Devils a la Champions
articles.summary: La leyenda del United analiza en MARCA la vuelta de los Red Devils a la Champions
articles.body: Dwight Yorke, mítico delantero del Manchester United del triplete (1998-2002) espera que el regreso de los suyos a la Champions tras dos años les coloque al menos entre los ocho mejores de Europa. Empezó con 4-0 al modesto Sabah de Azerbaiyán, pero ahora toca el primer toro de la tarde, el Atleti. Presente en la legendaria final Copa de Europa del 1999 disputada en el Camp Nou ante el Bayern de Munich, Yorke formaba un gran dúo ofensivo junto a Andy Cole, que ganó además tres títulos de campeón de Inglaterra (1999, 2000, 2001) y un triplete, el primero para un equipo de las Islas. Con los 'reds', anotó 64 goles en 151 partidos. Además fue el capitán del equipo de Trinidad y Tobago en el Mundial de Alemania 2006 y seleccionador de su país hasta marzo de este mismo año. Yorke pasó la mayor parte de su carrera en la Premier League: Aston Villa, United, Blackburn, Birmingham y Sunderland. Retirado a los 38 años y hoy embajador de Reviant, responde a MARCA sobre sus ex, el fútbol inglés, el español... Pregunta. Antes de analizar al United y aunque ya ha llovido, ¿la final del 99 con el Bayern es el mejor recuerdo de su vida? Respuesta. Toda aquella temporada fue increíble la verdad, y especialmente la forma en que llegamos hasta la final contra el Bayern. Desde luego, no fue nuestra mejor actuación del año, pero es la que la gente más asocia con nosotros. Nos convirtió en el primer equipo en ganar el triplete en el fútbol inglés; fue sensacional. No creo que las palabras puedan describir esa sensación. Es una sensación única para un grupo único de jugadores. Los jugadores que lo han conseguido con otros equipos entenderán perfectamente de lo que estoy hablando. Teníamos un equipo con auténtica calidad y un entrenador en su mejor momento, y los jugadores le seguían. Teníamos un equipo completo, con jugadores de talento en todas las posiciones, pero lo más importante es que teníamos la mentalidad ganadora necesaria para seguir adelante y ganarlo todo. P. Y además el triplete y entrar en la historia R. Fue algo extraño, único. Solo hay unos pocos jugadores que puedan contar cómo es un año en el que se gana el triplete o siquiera imaginarse cómo es. Además era mi primera temporada en el United tras un fichaje muy caro que mucha gente pensaba que no estaría a la altura. Tuve que adaptarme a eso muy rápidamente, no tuve tiempo de aclimatarme. Acepté el reto, estuve a la altura... No podría haber pedido un mejor momento para fichar por el United. Si alguien me pregunta por qué dejé el Villa, fue para ganar grandes competiciones. Ganar las tres ese año, ser el máximo goleador y ser elegido Jugador del Año, todo de una sola vez… No se puede pedir nada mejor. P. El United vuelve a la Champions, de donde nunca debió irse, ¿con qué papel se conforma el aficionado... o estrellas como Ud? R. Hay mucho potencial, pero hay que ir paso a paso. Teniendo en cuenta cómo ha empezado la temporada (13º en la Premier de momento), al Manchester United le valdría con llegar a cuartos de final en estos momentos. Hace tiempo que no nos encontramos en esa situación, no hemos tenido esa sensación de bienestar que supone estar en la Liga de Campeones. En todo caso, sabemos que eso no solo supondrá un nuevo impulso para el club desde el punto de vista económico, sino que, sin duda, a la hora de atraer a jugadores, el United ha vuelto al gran escenario, que es donde queremos estar. Llevamos un par de temporadas sin Champions, pero aquí estamos de nuevo. Tenemos que dar una buena imagen de lo que representa el Manchester United y recuperar esa regularidad de estar en las grandes competiciones. Así que, insisto, llegar a cuartos sería un logro increíble para nosotros y, sin duda, un paso adelante... Ganar la competición sería fantástico, pero de momento no lo veo posible. P. Se ha ido Casemiro... pero vuelve Rashford, hay repuntes, pero no parece arrancar la cosa. R. No veo por qué no se querría contar con alguien como Marcus Rashford. Considero que sigue siendo el mejor jugador del club en cuanto a talento, un jugador maravilloso. Sé que hay opiniones encontradas sobre Marcus, pero solo hay una forma de responder a eso. Al fin y al cabo, tiene 28 años y, en términos futbolísticos, no parece mucho. Necesita volver a remontar el vuelo; si juega en el United y vuelve a rendir bien, eso podría dar pie a otro traspaso para él, pero por ahora está aquí y tiene que dedicarse por completo al equipo. Si Marcus está totalmente concentrado, en forma y con muchas ganas de jugar, sigo pensando que es uno de nuestros jugadores ofensivos más contrastados en este equipo. P. ¿Y qué me dice de sus ex, Aston Villa, jugando esa Champions League como merecidos campeones de la Europa League? R. Creo que pasar de la fase de grupos y de la fase eliminatoria sería un logro enorme, teniendo en cuenta la transición por la que está pasando el Aston Villa. Están pasando muchas cosas allí; no se trata solo de uno o dos, sino de cinco o seis jugadores clave que se han marchado. Los jugadores que están fichando no tienen experiencia en competiciones europeas, y no estoy seguro de cómo se las arreglarán en todos los frentes. Pero si hay un hombre capaz de hacer que sean resistentes, competitivos y difíciles de batir, ese es el entrenador Unai Emery. P. El papel de Emery es evidente, como la 'españolización' del fútbol inglés, en técnicos y jugadores, es un hecho... ¿Qué tiene el fútbol español ahora mismo? Bueno, es algo cíclico, ¿no? Ha llevado su tiempo, pero ahora todos los clubes están fijándose en los entrenadores españoles y siguiendo la tendencia. Así es como funciona. Por desgracia, aquí en Inglaterra o en el Caribe, de momento no hemos sido capaces de formar a ese tipo de entrenadores. Y es fascinante ver que tenemos la mejor liga del mundo, pero que, aun así, Inglaterra tiene un entrenador extranjero. Eso dice mucho, aunque él no sea español, sino alemán. Pero eso te da una idea de en qué punto se encuentra el fútbol inglés. No me sorprende que todo el mundo esté siguiendo la tendencia española en este momento, porque con Rodri como mejor jugador del mundo y España ganando el Mundial, tienes a Pep, que podría decirse que es el mejor entrenador del mundo, tienes a Unai Emery y a algunos otros. Inglaterra tiene trabajo por delante. P. Media Premier estará jugando en Europa esta temporada, nueve equipos... pero no llega un título importante de los Three Lions… ¿qué ocurre? R. Inglaterra tiene trabajo por delante para que nuestro cuerpo técnico alcance el nivel de España. Si nos fijamos en los mejores equipos de Inglaterra, todos tienen entrenadores extranjeros. Aparte de Carrick, están Iraola en el Liverpool, Arteta en el Arsenal y Maresca en el City fíjate en su rendimiento. Eso nos indica que algo no va del todo bien en nuestra liga en lo que respecta a los entrenadores nacionales. Quizá sea hora de ver las cosas de otra manera, pero lo cierto es que los españoles están dominando en lo que se refiere al cuerpo técnico.

articles.title: Territorio Julián
articles.standfirst: La Champions en el Metropolitano, donde ha marcado 10 goles en 13 partidos, se presenta como el mejor escenario para su ‘indulto’
articles.summary: La Champions en el Metropolitano, donde ha marcado 10 goles en 13 partidos, se presenta como el mejor escenario para su ‘indulto’
articles.body: Primero fue escuchar a Simeone tenderle la mano desde lo deportivo. Después fue recibir el calor del vestuario con sus capitanes a la cabeza. Más tarde, la llegada de un Cuti Romero que acabó de brindarle la tranquilidad necesaria para recapacitar. Así que desde que asumió que la posición que había mantenido Miguel Ángel Gil durante todo el verano no era ningún farol y que el “sueño” de jugar en el Barcelona que le había metido su representante en la cabeza era imposible, Julián Alvarez no ha parado de enviar señales de su intención de volver a ser el que fue. Cierto es que por el camino ha tenido que sufrir cómo el Metropolitano le expresaba su repulsa por su afrenta veraniega tanto en la visita del Villarreal como en el derbi, pero sabe el delantero argentino que sólo existe una manera de conseguir su indulto: a base de actitud y goles. La primera premisa ya la ha dejado ver tanto en su primera titularidad en Liverpool, como en varias carreras ante el eterno rival que ya llegaron a tener reconocimiento desde la grada como el pasado sábado en Vitoria, donde se mostró participativo, con un disparo al palo incluido. Para el segundo supuesto, después de haber regresado a la senda del gol que no celebraba desde el Mundial en el reciente periplo con Argentina, Julián se agarra a su competición fetiche: la Champions. No hay que olvidar que, tras 17 goles en Europa, sólo Griezmann ha celebrado más como rojiblanco en el mayor torneo continental. De hecho, las cifras de Julián serían esenciales para alcanzar tanto los octavos, antes de ser víctima del doble toque, hace dos años como las semifinales del ejercicio pasado. Unos números que se disparan especialmente en el Metropolitano, pues en sus 13 partidos como local ha celebrado 10 dianas. Sin duda, el escenario perfecto para reencontrarse con un gol que no festeja de rojiblanco desde el lejano 29 de abril (precisamente ante el Arsenal en la Champions)... y que suponga el inicio de su redención

articles.title: Preparados para el infierno
articles.standfirst: El Barça busca mantener su excelente racha de triunfos en el campo del Galatasaray
articles.summary: El Barça busca mantener su excelente racha de triunfos en el campo del Galatasaray
articles.body: Jugar en Turquía nunca ha sido fácil. La presión que ejerce el público en los estadios es muy potente y supone un hándicap al que los equipos rivales deben sobreponerse. El Ali Sami Yen es uno de esos estadios. Desde que el mítico Dream Team perdiera allí frente al Galatasaray en un partido de Champions en los noventa, cada vez que los azulgranas visitan este campo tienen muy presente la dificultad que entraña. La realidad es que, en los últimos enfrentamientos, el Barcelona ha logrado superar al equipo turco, a pesar de estar muy bien arropado por sus fieles seguidores. Flick pretende que se mantenga la racha de los últimos tres partidos, en los que el Barcelona ha ganado en este estadio. A juzgar por el momento que atraviesa su equipo, lo lógico es pensar en un triunfo culé, ya que el conjunto azulgrana cuenta sus partidos por victorias. Sería la décima consecutiva, en un comienzo de temporada que no tiene parangón en la historia del club. Ni siquiera la ausencia de Raphinha debería ser un problema. El sábado, el equipo ya demostró que puede sobreponerse a la baja de su jugador más en forma. En esta liguilla de la Champions no hay excusas que valgan. Cada punto vale un potosí y los errores se pagan caros. El Barcelona tiene el objetivo de acabar primero o segundo en esta fase. Para conseguirlo, tendrá que ganar prácticamente todos sus partidos. Hace dos años, el equipo fue precisamente segundo, tras dejarse cinco puntos. La pasada campaña, la clasificación estuvo aún más cara. El Arsenal acabó primero tras ganar todos sus partidos, mientras que el Bayern fue segundo pese a perder solo uno. Enfrente tendrá a un equipo que necesita la victoria después de su derrota en la primera jornada frente al Sporting de Portugal. En sus filas militan jugadores importantes como Gündogan, que jugó una temporada en el Barcelona, Rafael Leão o el delantero Osimhen. Cualquiera de ellos es capaz de aguar la fiesta a los azulgranas. Por tanto, no caben las confianzas de cara al partido. Flick alineará al mejor equipo que tiene a su disposición, aunque sabe que debe dosificar a sus jugadores, ya que el calendario se vuelve cada vez más exigente.

articles.title: Mourinho, más ruido que juego
articles.summary: Al otro lado del espejo
articles.body: Mourinho regresó al Madrid con el aire beatífico del hombre que desde el sexto piso de la vida ya contempla las cosas con sosiego. Bastantes recelaban de esa nueva versión zen del que habíamos conocido como un hombre proclive a la bronca, y hasta diré que lo echaban de menos. Sus partidarios extrañaban el líder tras el que alinearse en causas atrabiliarias, los adversarios se desconcertaron ante ese hombre sosegado, sospechando una impostura; deseaban ver al tipo brusco y bronco que desacreditaba con sus gestos, palabras y actitudes al Madrid. Ahora, uno y otro sector han recuperado lo que tuvieron. Mourinho vuelve a ser ‘aquel’. Yo, sinceramente. creí en su intención de cambio, y me lo represento como alguien que ha tratado de quitarse del tabaco y al final se ha rendido, volviendo a las dos cajetillas diarias. Una lástima. No ha encontrado el juego y se ha replegado a sus viejas posiciones, demostrando que mantiene íntegra su capacidad para dictar la agenda. Un partido en cierto modo menor, ganado por 1-0 en casa, lo ha convertido en una tormenta a raíz de una jugada que era expulsión tan de catálogo que el propio Vinicius, cuando lo comprendió, emitió un mensaje pidiendo perdón a la afición y al equipo por su actitud. Sobre la incomodidad larvada por el ‘caso Negreira’, que a Florentino sólo se ha urgido combatir cuando comprobó (el marido siempre es el último en enterarse) que el Barça le estaba toreando con la Superliga, más la incesante actividad artillera de RMTV, Mourinho vuelve a levantar la bandera del victimismo. No acudió a la conferencia de prensa porque, hizo deslizar, no le hubieran dejado después sentarse en el banquillo ni ante el Sevilla ni ante el Barça. Cosa que no es cierta: por muchos disparates que dijera, la sanción hubiera sido recurrida y apelada con seguridad. Bien, se podía esperar esto de Mourinho. Fuimos ingenuos los que creíamos en que triunfaría en su batalla contra el tabaco. Pero lo que no se podía esperar era que después de compartir con el club la decisión de no fichar a Rodri no tuviera un plan para organizar un buen equipo sin él.

articles.title: Más fútbol y menos tirones de pelo
articles.summary: A ver qué se cuenta...
articles.body: Tiene razón, y mucha, el Real Madrid en reclamar urgentemente que se esclarezca el ‘caso Negreira’. Y hasta puede tener razón que en algunas ocasiones, no tantas, los arbitrajes no favorecen –es más, perjudican– a los madridistas. Y hasta puede tener razón en quejarse de horarios y un sinfín de cosas, muchas irrelevantes, pero que en ocasiones benefician a otros equipos. Todo cierto, pero la clave está en el fútbol que desarrolla el Real Madrid, decepcionante hasta el momento. La llegada de Mourinho invitaba a pensar que el Real Madrid jugaría con intensidad, fuerza, goles y un juego que ilusionaría, emocionaría y gustaría a los aficionados. Hasta el momento, esto no se ha visto y lleva camino a corto plazo de que no cambiará. ¿Culpa de Mourinho? ¿De los jugadores de la plantilla? La verdad es que el gran problema que tiene el Real Madrid es de fútbol y, otro, lo bien que lo juega el Barcelona. Es el problema del Real Madrid, que el equipo catalán arrasa, por lo menos en la Liga. Hace bien el equipo que preside Florentino Pérez en protestar por los arbitrajes de la Liga y justificar derrotas pero ahora viene la Champions y los árbitros son diferentes, los mejores del mundo, y ahora es cuando veremos al Real Madrid de verdad y que nos ha vendido Mourinho como un equipo que puede y debe aspirar a todo. En Europa no se puede culpar a los árbitros ni a Negreira de los malos resultados. Eso sí, en la Champions están Barcelona, PSG y Atlético, entre otros excelentes equipos, y con buenos árbitros, y Mourinho no tendrá excusas. Eso sí, necesita que el Real Madrid juegue mucho mejor de lo que lo está haciendo en la Liga y sin tirones de pelo. articles.title: Ronaldo scores amid Riyadh security scare to close in on 1,000 career goals, but Portugal disciplinary storm refuses to fade
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo continued his relentless pursuit of 1,000 career goals by scoring his 981st strike in professional football, helping Al-Nassr secure a
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo continued his relentless pursuit of 1,000 career goals by scoring his 981st strike in professional football, helping Al-Nassr secure a 3-1 victory over Uzbekistan's Neftchi Fergana in the AFC Champions League Elite on Monday. But the Portuguese superstar's latest goal came on a night when football briefly took a back seat to security concerns in Riyadh, while the disciplinary controversy surrounding his departure from Portugal's national team camp remained unresolved.The match at Al-Awwal Park was delayed by an hour after Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence issued a security alert shortly before the scheduled kick-off. The warning followed reports of ballistic missiles launched towards Riyadh by Yemen-based Houthi rebels, with the Saudi-led coalition saying it had intercepted and destroyed missiles targeting the capital. Explosions were also heard in the city before authorities subsequently announced that the danger had passed.Despite the unsettling circumstances and the wait to get the match underway, Al-Nassr eventually delivered on the pitch. Angelo Gabriel opened the scoring before Ronaldo doubled the advantage, with the 41-year-old once again demonstrating his ability to remain decisive in front of goal.The victory also provided a sporting boost for Ronaldo as he continues to chase one of football's most remarkable individual milestones, even as questions over his international future remain in the spotlight.Ronaldo strikes again as 1,000-goal milestone gets closerAl-Nassr took the lead in the 33rd minute when Angelo found the net with a deflected strike. Nine minutes later, Ronaldo doubled the advantage with a superb finish that underlined his instincts inside the penalty area.The move began with Sadio Mane delivering a looping cross from the left. Aiman Yahya directed the ball into Ronaldo's path with his chest, allowing the Portuguese forward to strike on the turn and send a powerful effort into the bottom corner.It was Ronaldo's 981st career goal across club and international football, leaving him 19 short of reaching the landmark of 1,000. At 41, the former Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus forward continues to add to a scoring record built over more than two decades at the highest level.Neftchi attempted to fight their way back into the contest when Alisher Odilov reduced the deficit six minutes into the second half. The visitors, however, suffered a major setback when Ikromjon Alibaev was sent off in the 65th minute for a foul on Mohamed Simakan.Al-Nassr capitalised on their numerical advantage when Anvarjon Gofurov put the ball into his own net in the 78th minute, restoring the Saudi side's two-goal cushion and sealing a 3-1 victory.Ronaldo later celebrated the result on Instagram, posting: "Important win tonight. We keep building."Portugal controversy continues after national-team walkoutRonaldo's return to club football has coincided with a disciplinary dispute involving the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF), which provisionally suspended the forward after opening proceedings over his departure from the national-team camp.The controversy followed Portugal's recent UEFA Nations League fixtures. Ronaldo was left unused during a victory over Norway after warming up with the expectation that he might feature. He subsequently left the squad's base in Copenhagen before Portugal's match against Denmark, amid a disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus over his role and playing time.Ronaldo reportedly felt that an understanding about his involvement had not been honoured. The dispute escalated when he left the camp, prompting the federation to initiate disciplinary proceedings.The FPF's disciplinary council subsequently imposed a non-automatic provisional suspension and classified the case as urgent. The measure is preliminary, with the investigation intended to establish whether Ronaldo's actions warrant a further sanction.Under the disciplinary regulations cited in reports, a player who leaves a national-team camp without justification can face a suspension ranging from one month to six months, alongside a financial penalty.The relevant provision states: "Any player who, after being lawfully called up, leaves without justification or does not attend a training session, a match, or any national team activity, or anything connected to the sporting representation of the Portuguese Football Federation or Portugal, shall be punished with a suspension ranging between one month and six months, and in addition, if the player is a professional, with a fine ranging between 5 and 10 accounting units."The potential consequences have placed Ronaldo's international future under renewed scrutiny. The forward remains Portugal's all-time leading scorer, and his desire to continue representing his country has not disappeared. However, the disciplinary process means that the episode cannot simply be dismissed as a disagreement over selection.There have also been signs that the door remains open for reconciliation, with Portuguese football officials and the coaching camp expressing a desire to resolve the situation. Nevertheless, the formal proceedings leave the question of any final punishment outstanding.A prolific scorer amid uncertainty over his international futureFor Ronaldo, the timing presents a striking contrast. At club level, he continues to deliver goals and move closer to a four-figure career tally. Away from Al-Nassr, however, his relationship with Portugal's setup faces a difficult period following the walkout and the subsequent disciplinary action.His goal against Neftchi was therefore significant for more than the result. It reinforced the forward's continued productivity at an advanced stage of his career while providing a reminder of the standards he has maintained across different leagues and competitions.The security delay also added an unusual backdrop to the contest. Players and spectators had to wait for confirmation that the situation was safe before the match could proceed, and the teams then had to refocus on the task at hand. articles.title: Bruno Fernandes: Is form of Man Utd captain symptom or reason for their form?
articles.summary: Manchester United skipper Bruno Fernandes is yet to reach the highs of last season - is it because of his side's poor start or the reason for it?
articles.body:
It is only seven weeks since Bruno Fernandes stood in the Manchester Opera House and spoke of his pride at being named PFA Player of the Year for 2025-26.

The Manchester United captain had already won the Premier League and Football Writers' versions, in recognition of the phenomenal contribution to his side's unexpected third-place finish.

Fernandes scored nine goals and claimed 21 assists, breaking a Premier League record jointly held by Thierry Henry and Kevin de Bruyne that had stood for 23 years.

Over the final 11 games of the season, of the 21 goals United scored, Fernandes either found the net himself or created 12 of them. In the seven-game run that swept United back into Europe's elite club competition after a two-year absence, the 31-year-old was a central figure in nine out of 12 goals. Statistically, it was remarkable, reminiscent of Eric Cantona in the 1995-96 title-winning campaign when he scored in six successive games, five of them when United only scored once.

"It was a special season for me," Fernandes told an appreciative audience. "I am very proud.

"But we don't play tennis. We don't play just for ourselves. We play for a team, we play for a club, we play for the fans. There is nothing more special than that."

Those words have particular resonance now because, compared with those exceptional statistics, there are some far less impressive ones this season.

Fernandes has played for every minute of Manchester United 's six Premier League games. He has three goals and one assist, all of which came against Ipswich, the second game of the campaign and, so far, his side's only win.

The numbers are actually better than last term, when he scored twice in the opening six games and failed to create any.

However, at that point, Fernandes was playing in the deeper midfield role Ruben Amorim preferred.

While this season is Fernandes' second highest for actual shots, at an average of 3.3 per game - his best was 3.5 in 2020-21 - it is his joint-second lowest for shots on target, at an average of 0.8. His chance creation (2.5 per game on average) is also the second lowest of his time at Old Trafford and down significantly on the 4.0 he returned last season.

Even more startlingly, he has created just one 'big chance' so far this season, the lofted pass that sent Bryan Mbeumo running clear of the Ipswich defence on 30 August. Fernandes' average last season was one per game.

A combination of Fernandes' numbers and his general involvement perhaps goes some way to explaining why United have collected just six points from their opening six games, their worst start to a league campaign in 40 years, when Ron Atkinson was eventually sacked to make way for Sir Alex Ferguson.

But is Fernandes a reason for, or a symptom of, United's malaise?

There is uncertainty over the Portugal playmaker's fitness. Fernandes rarely misses a game but was left out of the recent Nations League encounter with Norway as national team boss Jorge Jesus said the former Sporting man was "playing through pain".

However, Fernandes was fit enough to return for the final two internationals of the extended break. Prior to that, he completed the full 90 minutes in the 4-0 win against Azerbaijani champions Sabah FK in the Champions League.

United manager Michael Carrick does not view it as an issue.

"He was carrying something but that happens a lot," he said. "Players play with issues.

"It's not ideal but it is manageable. Bruno is able to play. That is the commitment he has got.

"He is pretty much over it, was really bright in training this morning and is looking forward to the game."

Towards the end of last season, when Fernandes' contribution was at its most prolific, Benjamin Sesko was a regular in the number nine role, while veteran Brazilian Casemiro was the anchor in United's midfield.

Of the nine league goals Sesko has scored in 2026, Fernandes created four. Fernandes was responsible for four of the final five goals Casemiro scored as a Manchester United player from 1 February onwards.

Quite aside from goals, it is also clear the presence of Sesko and Casemiro is being missed.

Even Casemiro's biggest admirers could not claim United's current low running stats are because the 34-year-old left for Inter Miami in the summer. However, his positioning and game knowledge remain of a high standard. Fernandes could take risks in the belief United would not be overrun on transition if he lost the ball.

As for Sesko, his fresh shin injury merely extends a lack of involvement which is being keenly felt and for which, as yet, there is no end date.

The club's power brokers ignored a clamour to bring in more striking support in the summer and instead reinforced Carrick's midfield.

But a plan to cover the Slovenian's initial absence by using Mbeumo as a number nine had to be scrapped when Amad Diallo suffered an ankle injury just before the opening game at Hull.

Matheus Cunha was given the job instead, but he repeatedly dropped deep, right into the space Fernandes was occupying, and the pair never really found an effective way of dealing with it.

For Fernandes, it feels restrictive, and while he is not a player who lacks confidence, it does seem his decision-making is being affected.

Against Tottenham at the weekend, it took Fernandes an incredible 23 minutes just to complete a pass.

Carrick said on Monday, as he looked ahead to a meeting with Atletico Madrid, that no-one was "guaranteed" a place in his team - but put enough caveats around it to indicate leaving out his captain is not in his thinking.

However, United must start to improve and, that means Fernandes must do the same.

"Sometimes things don't quite go for you. Sometimes you have a spell of that.

"But he's done some incredible things for this football club and he will do the same in the future, there's no doubt about that."

articles.title: Liverpool set to replace faltering star in January
articles.summary: Liverpool’s start to life under Andoni Iraola has been somewhat disappointing. The Reds find themselves in ninth place after six games, behind Everton, Leeds...
articles.body:
Liverpool's start to life under Andoni Iraola has been somewhat disappointing.

The Reds find themselves in ninth place after six games, behind Everton, Leeds and Hull City, having only won twice in the league so far.

Although Iraola's side have struggled to find consistency anywhere on the pitch, one of the most frustrating positions has been right-back.

With Conor Bradley still sidelined by an injury he picked up in January, and Jeremie Frimpong failing to impress at any point this season, Ronald Araujo has found himself as the makeshift first-choice on the right side of Liverpool's backline.

As Iraola's issues pile up concerns over Frimpong's ability could lead to a January transfer.

Since arriving from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer of 2025, Frimpong has failed to nail down a starting place in Liverpool's XI.

When Trent Alexander-Arnold, the club's previous long-time starter, left the club weeks before Frimpong was signed many assumed that the Dutchman would be the automatic replacement.

Even under Arne Slot the 25-year-old couldn't cement his place, with Bradley, Curtis Jones and Dominik Szoboszlai all playing significant minutes at right-back.

Now, after only one full season, the club are reportedly willing to move on from Frimpong and the Dutchman could be replaced as soon as this winter.

That's according to a report from Football Insider , which claims the recruitment team at Anfield have now begun looking for a replacement.

The report states that other issues with Iraola's squad could push right-back recruitment down the list of priorities, especially if Bradley returns to training before the New Year, so a deal for Frimpong's replacement may have to wait until the summer.

There has also been some reported interest in the Dutchman which could lead to an early departure, in which case an addition at fullback would jump to top priority.

An exit isn't guaranteed this winter but, with other clubs already interested and Liverpool ready to move on, Frimpong's days at Anfield could be numbered.

articles.title: Coventry 4 Newcastle 1 match ratings and comments on all Newcastle United players
articles.summary: We asked Davey Hat-Trick to give us his match ratings and player comments after Coventry 4 Newcastle 1 in the Premier League. Before this game, I was joking...
articles.body:
We asked Davey Hat-Trick to give us his match ratings and player comments after Coventry 4 Newcastle 1 in the Premier League.

Before this game, I was joking to may mates that as Coventry had only scored one goal this season, we should all put our money on a thumping home win. It turns out I have no sense of humour.

Newcastle came to Coventry with something to prove to me.

Willock for Dedić (and the subsequent shift in position for Miley) aside, this was the same starting XI that did so poorly in our last away match at Leeds. They did just as badly tonight.

You could argue – with a degree of veracity – that Newcastle had more of the play and controlled large parts of this game. But where it matters, we were very, very poor. We wasted good chances and conceded poor goals.

Coventry played like a team with belief; Newcastle looked like they lack confidence. We need to get that back quickly. If we don't, things could get hairy.

Most Newcastle United fans, I think, would tolerate a season of mid-table mediocrity. We've had a major upheaval in personnel, and it will take time for things to click, especially with such a young squad. But we looked like a team in relegation form tonight and that was against a newly-promoted team who lost their first four games.

If Newcastle United had won tonight, we'd have gone fourth. We never looked like doing that.

A horrendous error of judgement in the first five minutes, conceding a penalty that he really didn't need to.

Coventry scored and that set the tone for the rest of the game. Couldn't do much about the other goals, and to be fair to him, he's decent with the ball at his feet. But a performance like this makes those around him nervous.

A couple of decent tackles but he doesn't look like a right back.

Murphy was cutting inside and I was expecting Lewis to overlap him. I didn't see it

A couple of poor clearances, one of which led to Coventry's second goal. Couldn't wait to give Joelinton the captain's armband when the latter took to the field.

Made a hash of things at the back more than once but scored the goal of the game with a thumping drive.

I seem to keep giving Lewis a higher mark than his team mates. But that is only because he is usually our best player.

I thought he was again tonight, albeit with no one really pushing him for that honour. Didn't get everything right but showed tenacity and drive that his colleagues lacked

I have said this before – probably after the Leeds game – and I'll repeat it here. A two-man midfield is doing us no favours at all, especially away from home.

Nico is a good player who looked in control when we were in possession (and will be credited with an assist tonight!), but he was chasing shadows whenever Coventry came at us.

Tried hard but never seemed to get on top of things.

He's been good so far this season but he was poor tonight. Missed a couple of presentable chances.

Got a couple of decent balls into the box – one was an absolute peach that should have led to a goal – but wasn't much of a threat otherwise.

I'd be surprised if he starts on Saturday.

Never looked like threatening the Coventry goal, despite a lot of effort on his part.

Didn't look good on Coventry's second goal. I know he's not a defender but I thought he could have closed their man down better than he did.

A frustrating performance. Kept running into trouble.

Appealed for a couple of penalties he was never going to get. He can do much better than this.

Some glimpses of his potential were there for everyone to see.

He's lightning fast but he repeatedly made poor decisions when he had the ball in the first half.

You could see the confidence draining out of him. He was so anonymous after the break I thought we'd subbed him off. Needs time, encouragement and an arm round his shoulder.

Joelinton 4 We looked a little less fragile for a while when big Joe entered the fray.

But he overplayed in his own penalty area and was dispossessed for Coventry's third. That ended the game as a contest.

Showed promise in our first few games but seems to be less assured now. Played with a scowl on his face.

Did a lot better than most when he came on down the right.

He'd have had a better score if he learned to pass instead of shoot on occasion. I was thinking he'd be a shoo-in to take Murphy's place on Saturday but he took a nasty blow on his ankle which saw him come off. Looks like a good signing.

Didn't do much in his 15 minutes but I'm not sure that is relevant in the grand scheme of things.

Last season he was something of a peripheral figure, although he finished strongly.

This season he's going to have to take a lot of responsibility for scoring and assisting. We'll see how he rises to the challenge.

articles.title: An insurance policy with no guarantee - the complex issue of egg-freezing in sport
articles.summary: BBC Sport examines the potential benefits, risks and unanswered questions facing female athletes about egg-freezing.
articles.body:
"I remember waking up in the morning and I couldn't stand. I was bent over in two. I could barely walk."

For Geva Mentor - England netball's most decorated player - this was the reality of going through the process of having her eggs frozen in 2019.

"I had just played in my fourth World Cup and I was at a bit of a loss in terms of where my life was going personally, as I always wanted a family," Mentor tells BBC Sport.

Egg-freezing is a process in which a woman's eggs are collected, frozen and stored for potential use later in life.

While Mentor's decision was a deeply personal one, the issue is becoming increasingly visible in elite sport, with both Chelsea and the Spanish Football Federation recently announcing support for players wanting to freeze their eggs.

It is often presented as a way for women to help preserve their fertility and, in some cases, delay motherhood. For female athletes, whose careers often peak in the years they are most fertile, the appeal can be particularly powerful.

"I wanted to go through a check-up and make sure things weren't drying up down there, so to speak, because I didn't know what impact elite sport might have had on my fertility," says Mentor.

"Freezing my eggs seemed like the right thing to do at the time because [I thought] whatever happens with my journey, I'd rather use my early 30-year-old eggs than my late-30s or 40s."

Mentor is one of a growing number of athletes to consider fertility preservation during their careers, but the practice remains the subject of debate and experts stress it offers no guarantee of a future pregnancy.

Mentor is widely regarded as netball's greatest ever goal keeper, winning 175 international caps. She represented England at six World Cups, winning a silver and three bronze medals, and was part of the Roses side that won Commonwealth gold in 2018.

For 20 years, being an elite athlete was her every focus. However, she always knew she wanted to be a mother and worried about when that would come.

At the age of 35 she decided to freeze her eggs in the hope it may help her conceive in the future.

Mentor was not in a relationship at the time, and living in Melbourne.

"I decided that I wanted to do it in off-season, going into pre-season, and not during the season," she says.

"I thought that if anything untoward happened, I'd have that time and space to let my body recover before I'd have to sort of throw it into elite training."

Mentor had regular monitoring appointments throughout the treatment.

"I still trained, did pre-season," she adds. "It didn't affect me at all until I took the last reactive injection, which basically releases the eggs into position for extraction the next day."

Egg retrieval is performed under sedation or general anaesthetic and typically takes 15-30 minutes.

Mentor says it felt like she had "43 golf balls shoved in my lower region" as the fertility drugs she had taken had stimulated a large number of eggs, which were then retrieved.

"They pierced my vaginal wall 43 times, which meant that I was probably on a bit of a risk for bleeding and blood clots," she said.

"One of the things that really stood out for me was when I came around and I immediately just started crying... like bawling. It was quite emotional. What you're going through, that whole process, there's a lot of a hormone change and imbalance. I guess it really just shook me.

"But then I knew at the end of the day, it was an insurance policy for me."

Mentor was released from hospital the same day but was unable to return to full training for two weeks as she recovered from experiencing heavy bleeding.

She has since had a daughter after conceiving naturally but says she has no regrets about freezing her eggs, which remain available for her to use in the future.

While many have hailed fertility support for female athletes as a major step forward, one world-leading expert in women's health says important questions still remain.

Professor Kirsty Elliott-Sale, who heads the Centre for Excellence for Women in Sport at Manchester Metropolitan University, says she is "delighted for any player who will benefit" from fertility support.

But she believes egg-freezing should be seen as one option among a wider package of support for female athletes, and urges those considering it to look beyond the headlines - and ask plenty of questions.

"Egg-freezing is an opportunity which allows them to invest in their fertility journey - at this moment - for the future," she tells BBC Sport.

"But we need to make sure that if they want to have children during their careers, that is an opportunity for them."

Elliott-Sale says fertility, pregnancy and maternity provision must be as well funded as egg-freezing, so there is never a conversation that starts with: "Oh, but you froze your eggs..."

She also warns that egg-freezing should not be seen as a guarantee of future motherhood.

The number and quality of eggs collected can vary, some may not survive thawing, and those that do may fail to fertilise. Even when embryos develop, implantation and pregnancy are not assured.

There are also unanswered questions about how treatment fits around the demands of elite sport.

"One of the things that none of us know right now is how long you should take away from sport, if indeed you need to take any time away from sport to do this procedure," she says.

Elliott-Sale also wants clarity about what happens after eggs have been stored.

"It's one thing to fund the freezing," she says, questioning whether clubs will also pay for their storage then the treatment needed to use them.

And there's an anti-doping consideration, too.

Fertility drugs that are used to stimulate egg production for retrieval and freezing are banned by the World Anti-Doping Agency.

Athletes must therefore declare them and seek a Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE), which gives them permission to take a prohibited substance for a specified time.

'You can't simply pause your career to become a mother'

Chelsea say their support extends beyond egg-freezing alone.

BBC Sport understands the club's fertility fund is worth £189,000, shared between 27 players - equivalent to £7,000 each.

A cycle of egg-freezing typically costs about £3,350, plus medication and ongoing storage fees. The full process, including thawing and embryo transfer, can cost £7,000-£8,000, according to UK regulator the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority.

Former Chelsea goalkeeper Carly Telford, now a commercial manager at the club, says players can access a range of services - from fertility testing and egg-freezing to IVF treatment.

"The players will have their own pot of money that's for them to use and dip into whenever they like," Telford said in an interview with CBS.

Players also have direct access to doctors and the clinic.

"I really hope that more clubs are looking at it," she added. "It's important for us to make sure we can be there and catch them when they need something else from us other than the football."

Spain international Alexia Putellas, meanwhile, welcomed her federation's fertility initiative as a "huge step forward".

Speaking to El Pais last month, she said: "The federation understands that you're serving your country at the expense of your biological clock… that you can't simply pause your career to become a mother because you need your body to do your job."

But Spanish Olympic triple jumper Ana Peleteiro-Compaore Brion questioned the motivation for the support.

"Is this measure intended to make it easier for women to be mothers or is it intended to make it easier for them not to be while they're playing?" she wrote on Instagram.

Elliott-Sale says the offer must be voluntary, properly explained and part of broader maternity support.

"I think for sure it's a great offer, it's a great choice and opportunity, but it needs to go alongside other considerations," she says.
