articles.title: UCLA coach Bob Chesney: 'Serious concern' QB Nico Iamaleava could miss season
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES (AP) — UCLA coach Bob Chesney says there's “serious concern” that quarterback Nico Iamaleava could miss the rest of the season with a knee injury...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — UCLA coach Bob Chesney says there's "serious concern" that quarterback Nico Iamaleava could miss the rest of the season with a knee injury.

The 22-year-old was hurt just before halftime of the Bruins' 17-15 victory over Oregon on Saturday when he scrambled for a first down and was sandwiched between two defenders.

"I'm going to wait for our doctors to make the final call," Chesney said Monday at his weekly news conference. "There is some serious concern at the moment. But at the same point in time, there's nothing that has been fully ruled at this moment. There's still other opinions and other people we want to talk to, to make sure everyone sees it the same way."

The No. 12 Bruins (5-0, 3-0 Big Ten) host Wisconsin (4-1, 2-0) Saturday at the Rose Bowl.

Iamaleava has thrown four touchdowns, four interceptions and completed 62.1% of his attempts for 982 yards on the season. He's also a threat as part of the Bruins' rushing attack in his second season in Westwood since transferring from Tennessee.

Backup Ty Dieffenbach replaced Iamaleava in the second half and threw for 43 yards and a touchdown against the Ducks. Sophomore Madden Iamaleava, Nico's younger brother, is another option at QB for the Bruins. Neither backup has started a Football Subdivision Game.

articles.title: Real Madrid legend hits out at Barcelona defensive star over refereeing controversy: ‘They are afraid to speak’
articles.summary: Real Madrid have been in the midst of a refereeing saga in recent weeks, with the club disappointed by decisions going against them in their recent La Liga e...
articles.body:
Real Madrid have been in the midst of a refereeing saga in recent weeks, with the club disappointed by decisions going against them in their recent La Liga encounters.

Jose Mourinho came to the press conference after the Madrid derby with photographs of challenges against his team that went unpunished.

He then decided to avoid the press conference altogether, fearing a suspension after the red card that Vinicius Junior received against Villarreal.

Now, Real Madrid legend Roberto Carlos has questioned the reluctance of professional footballers to speak openly about refereeing controversies.

His comments appear to be aimed at Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi following the youngster's response to Madrid's complaints.

Roberto Carlos questions players' willingness to speak

As quoted by laSexta Deportes , the former Brazil international, who now serves as a Real Madrid ambassador, criticised the lack of unity among professional players.

"Professional players are not united. They are afraid to speak," Roberto Carlos declared.

Cubarsi was asked about the situation in Barcelona's press conference ahead of facing Galatasaray.

"I don't focus on that issue, but on what I can do something about, which is my club, what we can give to our people," Cubarsi said.

The 19-year-old's response did not acknowledge the problem in La Liga or the inconsistency in refereeing decisions.

Carlos' criticism also raises questions about whether players from rival clubs should remain silent when refereeing controversies involve teams other than their own.

Real Madrid's refereeing frustrations continue

The debate comes shortly after Madrid's controversial 1-0 victory over Villarreal, which included Vinicius Junior receiving a straight red card for pulling an opponent's hair.

The Brazilian also had a goal disallowed following a VAR review, adding to the frustration surrounding the match.

Vinicius' dismissal has also revived discussions about consistency in refereeing decisions, particularly after his representatives highlighted a previous incident involving Stole Dimitrievski.

Roberto Carlos makes an important point. Refereeing standards should not become a concern only when a particular club feels disadvantaged.

Real Madrid are right to want the refereeing to improve in La Liga. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

More professional footballers should be willing to speak openly when they believe decisions are inconsistent, regardless of whether those decisions affect Real Madrid, Barcelona or another La Liga side.

Remaining silent simply because a controversy involves a rival does little to improve the league.

Cubarsi is entitled to focus on Barcelona, but Roberto Carlos is right to suggest that greater unity could make the players' collective voice more influential.

If more players speak out constructively, La Liga could face greater pressure to improve transparency, clarify its rules and ensure more consistent decisions.

Such changes would benefit the entire competition in the long run, and the ultimate goal should be an improvement in the refereeing system.

articles.title: Josh Allen, Bills win OT ‘MNF’ thriller against Rams
articles.summary: Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills proved to be unstoppable late in action against the Los Angeles Rams during Monday Night Football
articles.body:
Halfway through Monday Night Football, it appeared as though the primetime audience got a bit of a dud in Week 5. The Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams were too in their heads, trying to play a game of keep-away due to MVP quarterbacks Josh Allen and Matthew Stafford.

After Ray Davis' opening kick return of 70 yards, what unfolded early was downright ugly football. That's quite a feat given how little time Buffalo's offense had the ball. Right down to the arm punt to end the first half, things felt eerily similar to last Sunday. It seemed at that moment as though Josh Allen was broken.

Most people knew that if Buffalo was to win in Los Angeles, they'd have to put their spikes in and sprint to the finish on offense. Yet, at halftime it looked like the Bills were still in the sort of funk that allowed them to throw away a game to the New England Patriots in Week 4.

To be fair, Allen lacks the sort of riches Stafford has catching passes on a routine basis. That doesn't excuse the arm punts, which have officially re-entered "trend" territory. But just as was true of two fumbles by running back James Cook III, Allen's interception didn't cost the Bills a win. That's a trend Bills Mafia can rally around, if necessary.

There is much work to be done, however. That's true of the entire roster.

In that moment, Allen should have run for yards, or checked the ball down, or even out of bounds — anything other than heaving it into traffic. Live another down, run more clock, and make it that much harder on Stafford and company looking for quick points. Though, again, it ultimately didn't do the team harm.

At the half, it was a bit stunning to see the Bills were ahead. How many people do you think went to bed? They're in for quite a surprise when they wake up with the sun. But who could blame a person? Everything just felt off, yet familiar to what plagued them in last week's loss.

Then something clicked at halftime. Both teams came out firing, perhaps throwing a bit too much caution to the wind in key moments. Yet as I've already stated: No turnover decided the game.

Instead, we can look back at a pair of bold points I made pre-game . The Bills would probably need to convert a two-point conversion (and against a team near-equally woeful converting them), and they had to capitalize on special teams mistakes against a woeful Rams unit.

That first point proved a challenge once again, as Brady and the offense played it cute with so much goofy pre-snap motion that it led to a false start. There's too much thinking outside the box with their two-point offense. With Allen, the move should always be to run the ball or get him on the move and looking for Kincaid.

Well, they missed the first try, then made up for it later with a still-glitchy but successful try with a pass from Allen to Kincaid. More of that, with less glitch is a good idea. Brady's reaction was all you needed to see in understanding how big a moment it was to convert that two-point try.

As to the special teams point, it's a full course meal. Ray Davis was shot out of a cannon early as a kick returner. Had he not been caught from behind by a defensive lineman playing kicker, Davis was scoring on the first play. It wasn't ideal settling for a field goal after that return, but they proved to be important points.

Special teams would once again play a huge role late in overtime following Cook's second fumble. Rousseau once again coming up huge in the crunch, leaping to deflect the Rams' game-winning field goal attempt. Out of nowhere, the Bills had new life and no one was more relieved than Cook. (The Bills are 2-0 this season when Cook fumbles twice in a game.)

The football world knows what happens when you keep giving Josh Allen chances. If you were to try defending the idea of QB wins as a stat, all you'd need do now is play the tape of the Bills' final drive in overtime. Allen took complete control of the game, running through, around, and over any defender in his way. One man (and, yes, an offensive line) against 11 defenders.

Understanding the moment, once Allen got into Bass' comfortable field goal range, head coach Joe Brady wasn't leaving anything to foolish chance in order to create a more ideal scenario. Brady's hunch proved correct, and Bass walked off a hero who'd been given the keys to trust.

This is the type of win that could properly fuel the team. There's a lot of season left and they're certain to face similar or worse adversity. They played a heck of a game of chess against a Super Bowl favorite. Now the Bills need to get things figured out on defense, while continuing to capitalize on every bit of good luck that comes their way.

It's unfamiliar territory, to be sure, but winning in overtime looks great on Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills.

articles.title: Hansi Flick calls up Barcelona youth team forward for first-team training ahead of Galatasaray clash
articles.summary: Barcelona have handed Shane Kluivert a taste of first-team training in Istanbul, with Hansi Flick bringing the Juvenil A winger into the senior squad’s prepa...
articles.body:
Barcelona have handed Shane Kluivert a taste of first-team training in Istanbul, with Hansi Flick bringing the Juvenil A winger into the senior squad's preparations for the Champions League meeting with Galatasaray .

According to SPORT , the 19-year-old joined the session to help complete the tactical work ahead of Tuesday's fixture.

His inclusion, however, does not signal an immediate promotion, with the move understood to be temporary.

Kluivert is expected to return to Barcelona's youth setup for the UEFA Youth League meeting against Galatasaray, where he will be an important attacking option as the Catalans look to strengthen their European campaign.

Kluivert trains with Barcelona first team

The young winger's presence initially went unnoticed during Monday's training session in Istanbul.

Kluivert did not appear on the pitch during the first 15 minutes, open to the media, meaning his involvement was not immediately identified.

He was the only youth-team player called up to join the first-team group.

SPORT indicates that Flick's decision was primarily intended to provide the numbers required for the tactical session rather than signal a change in Kluivert's standing within the senior squad.

For Kluivert, it was still an opportunity that offers the youngster valuable exposure to Flick's methods and the demands of first-team preparation.

However, his immediate focus remains with the youth side rather than the senior team's Champions League plans.

Barcelona face Galatasaray with three injury absentees

Kluivert's involvement came as Barcelona finished preparing for a difficult European assignment.

Shane Kluivert trained with the first team, but will not play against Galatasaray. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

Flick has travelled to Istanbul with his available players , but three senior footballers remain sidelined through injury.

Raphinha is the most prominent absentee after returning early from Brazil's international camp with muscle oedema in his right thigh, sustained during the second friendly against Australia.

Frenkie de Jong and Andreas Christensen are also unavailable.

Meanwhile, Kluivert faces a separate European challenge, as Barcelona's Juvenil A side faces Galatasaray in the Youth League after stumbling against Feyenoord on the opening matchday.

The Dutch-born attacker is expected to return to that squad, where his contribution could be important to Barça's hopes of progressing.

articles.title: The star is Luis Enrique: Inside the plans to keep PSG at the top
articles.summary: As Luis Enrique bids to guide PSG to a third successive Champions League triumph, Guillem Balague looks at how the coach keeps his side at the top.
articles.body:
Johan Cruyff, a man Paris St-Germain boss Luis Enrique deeply admires, used to say the hardest thing in football is winning after winning.

This season has been designed by Luis Enrique at PSG with that conundrum in mind.

The back-to-back European champions could become only the second team to win three consecutive Champions Leagues this season. They are also aiming for a third successive league triumph.

They arrive at Etihad Stadium on Wednesday sixth in Ligue 1, with just three wins, two draws and one defeat. Nobody in Paris is panicking, though.

Luis Enrique's side made a similarly slow start last season, but the coach was confident the results would come.

"Do you want to bet against us?" he said recently.

Luis Enrique recently signed a contract until 2030, and so have a number of players central to his plan.

The big danger is that a group who have won everything will believe they can relax without anyone noticing.

Much of what he has done so far is about preventing exactly that.

Can PSG do a three-peat and win six trophies this season?

When the club announced his new contract, they also confirmed new deals for Joao Neves, Fabian Ruiz, Willian Pacho, Lucas Beraldo and Senny Mayulu, sending a clear message to the dressing room that this is still a long-term project.

There has been remarkably little change in the technical staff since Luis Enrique arrived at PSG in 2023.

Assistant Joaquin Valdes has been alongside Luis Enrique since their Barcelona B days, and he is the one who talks to the players on a personal level.

He also helps keep his boss grounded when Luis Enrique's mind drifts too far away, and you can see him in the background in every news conference.

Rafel Pol, who handles strategy and acts as second in command, is another constant presence.

Very little of the way they train on and off the pitch has altered during Luis Enrique's three years at the club.

The players aren't shown a huge amount of videos, but there is a big screen on the training pitch to correct players and two cranes for the coaches to see everything from a height.

The one real change though is in the luxury of depth - a factor that proved key last campaign.

Luis Enrique can now regularly leave out a couple of key players from his squad and the team does not suffer.

Ousmane Dembele was not in the squad for the win against Le Mans on Saturday, and earlier in the season it was Lucas Digne who was left out. Against the bigger opponents, such as Manchester City and Barcelona, the starters arrive rested.

Against Le Mans, he used eight players that would not start the bigger matches, and, with the match level, he brought on four of his 'stars' to ensure the win.

His attack has been renewed after Gonzalo Ramos, Bradley Barcola and Lee Kang-in all departed.

Dani Gil, Paris correspondent for the Spanish radio station COPE, explains: "Barcola could not be given the minutes he wanted, they had won everything and been paid well for it, and the club could do with players who were hungrier.

"Mika Godts and Ferran Torres fit that description. Neither has yet won at club level what the departed players won."

Barcola was not rated by the coaches as someone who could reach the level Dembele sets, yet his flashes of brilliance were enough to convince Liverpool to pay £123m for him.

Summer signing Torres is the more intriguing case. He went through a difficult stretch psychologically, worked on his mental strength and now calls himself 'the Shark'.

He was unhappy at Barcelona when he was not playing regularly, even though last season produced his best numbers.

Now, having netted the winner for Spain in the World Cup final, he has scored seven goals in France. For the first time in his career he feels really wanted.

He also knows what kind of team he has joined. In a Luis Enrique side the star is Luis Enrique, and the forward is content with that.

The way of playing, the standards, the habits, they all belong to the coach, and the players slot in.

It explains why the club could sell famous names without the team losing its identity.

Luis Enrique, who has taken a space that PSG's Qatari owners had never handed to any other coach, has turned a club once seen as a collection of expensive signings into one envied by the rest of the world, by signing wisely but also by drawing value from the academy.

Four homegrown players - Warren Zaire-Emery, Mayulu, Quentin Ndjantou and Ibrahim Mbaye - played in the Champions League last season.

The first-team headquarters sit at the top of a hill, and the academy is at the bottom, so the young players have to climb, literally and metaphorically, if they want to make it.

The campus was officially opened in November 2024 after an investment of 350m euros, and for the first time the professional teams, the men's and women's academies and the school all share one site.

The method is imposed from the top down. The under-23s coach is a former player, but the style comes from Luis Enrique's first team, with constant meetings between them and academy directors.

Yohan Cabaye, director of the training centre, speaks often to director of football Luis Campos and Olivier Gagne, the deputy director of professional football. Campos, Gagne and Luis Enrique attend youth league games whenever they can.

The recent international break showed that way of working. Only four first-team players remained at the club.

Sixteen academy players were away with their national teams too. Luis Enrique spent the three weeks on the training ground with the youngsters as they got the rare chance to impress the coach.

His relationship with the media is distant. When asked what he had done during the three-week break, he said it was of no interest to anyone.

It is his way of marking distance. He keeps friendships with two or three Spanish journalists, who might get an answer to a phone message, but in France he has drawn a firm line.

There is no 'off the record', no coffee with reporters and no one-to-one interviews for anyone. In his first year he answered in Spanish, and now he replies only in very good French.

Yet when football is the subject, he is very interesting.

Before the Le Mans game he opened by saying that, as usual, we worry about the most banal things in football. Then he explained how French perception works.

When PSG win, the rivals are considered inferior, but when they struggle, it is declared a catastrophe. He said the view from the media is always extreme.

It will be fascinating to see how Luis Enrique handles the subject of former manager Pep Guardiola, who will be present at the game , and the charges brought against City by the Premier League. My sense is that he will stand up for him.

There will obviously be a meeting between them, and that is Luis Enrique's way of saying something, not necessarily about the case itself but about what he thinks of Guardiola's legacy.

They know the questions may arrive in Manchester, but the PSG media team has no plan to prepare a coordinated response. That is how much they trust the manager.

Whatever he is asked, expect the same Luis Enrique: sharp, managing the pressure and comfortable at the top.

articles.title: Highly-rated Red earns first start: Predicted United line-up vs Atleti with Mainoo and Shaw ruled out
articles.summary: Manchester United have travelled to the Spanish capital and are preparing for their second Champions League group-phase tie this evening.The Red Devils lock...
articles.body:
Manchester United have travelled to the Spanish capital and are preparing for their second Champions League group-phase tie this evening.

The Red Devils lock horns with Atletico Madrid in an 8pm kick-off in hopes of overseeing a second successive UCL victory.

How the clubs are faring ahead of kick-off

United kicked off their European campaign with a comfortable 4-0 triumph over Azerbaijan outfit Sabah last month, and have had to wait just over a month before continuing their journey in the competition.

Fans are well aware that the fixture will be anything but an easy ride; not only because of how notoriously frustrating Atletico are to play against, but also because they have yet to taste defeat on home soil this season and are on a four-game winning streak heading into the clash.

Michael Carrick is having to make do without some of his most pivotal starters, having confirmed yesterday that Kobbie Mainoo and Luke Shaw had been ruled out.

Carrick asked whether Bruno Fernandes is carrying an injury:"He was carrying something [an injury]. It happens a lot, people don't realise it. I probably played 80% of the games through my career with issues. That's how it is.He is pretty much over it, but right now it's not… pic.twitter.com/DEmXVAExtB

They picked up injuries during the 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday, and were absent from the side's open training session on Monday morning .

United team news and predicted starting XI

Elsewhere, Benjamin Sesko remains sidelined.

Carrick also said in his pre-match press conference that, at present, he was unable to offer an estimated return timeframe for the Slovenian.

Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui both sustained injuries on international duty, meaning Carrick is without his only two senior left-backs and the option who'd be next in line to deputise (Mazraoui).

As a result, Diogo Dalot is poised to switch flanks and fill in for his sidelined teammates while Leny Yoro occupies the right-back role.

articles.title: 🗞️ A devilish matchday: Champions League dominates Tuesday's front pages
articles.summary: The Champions League returns to the spotlight with tough away trips for Barça and Atlético, while the 'Negreira case' and managerial upheaval dominate the he...
articles.body:
The Champions League returns to the spotlight with tough away trips for Barça and Atlético, while the 'Negreira case' and managerial upheaval dominate the headlines.

A challenge in hell and the 'Metropolitano effect'

The Champions League dominates the sports press. Marca dubs the matchday a "Devilish night", highlighting Barcelona 's visit to Galatasaray at Ali Sami Yen and the clash between Atlético de Madrid and Manchester United , with Julián Álvarez starting.

Meanwhile, Mundo Deportivo focuses on the "Challenge in hell" facing Flick 's side as they look to maintain their perfect winning record, and stresses Atlético's urgent need for a win after losing at Anfield.

Sport leads with "Going for the tenth" to capture Barça's winning streak, identifying the atmosphere in Istanbul as their biggest obstacle.

In Madrid, AS opts for an emphatic "Step right up" to set the stage for Barça, Atlético and Villarreal's return to European action.

In the Valencian and Andalusian press, Superdeporte declares Unbeatable! after the dramatic 3–3 draw between Levante and Sevilla, sealed in stoppage time.

articles.title: Real Madrid rejected two goalkeeper signings in the summer to back veteran star – report
articles.summary: Real Madrid’s number so far this season may not highlight Thibaut Courtois’ brilliance, but the fact of the matter is that the Belgian star has been simply s...
articles.body:
Real Madrid's number so far this season may not highlight Thibaut Courtois' brilliance, but the fact of the matter is that the Belgian star has been simply stellar.

Having just two clean sheets so far underplays his brilliance significantly, but it has more to do with the team's defensive lacunae.

Yesterday, word broke out that the Belgian star is set to renew his deal with Real Madrid and that an agreement in principle has been reached. Despite his age, after all, he continues to be one of the best goalkeepers in the world.

34 and going strong. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

As reported by Fabrizio Romano in a recent update, Real Madrid have been thinking about the goalkeeping situation for a while now, and agents of goalkeepers across the globe naturally have knowledge of the same.

In fact, the club have been offered two goalkeeper signings since the summer alone. However, they did not waste any time in rejecting the approaches.

Los Blancos maintained a strong response to the representatives of the said goalkeepers.

"We have the best goalkeeper in the world," they said, making it clear that they do not see a need to replace the veteran yet. Now, the player will stay at the club for longer after his renewal.

Courtois has renewed his contract. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

At 34 years of age, it is understandable that Real Madrid are only offering a renewal until 2027-28 to the player.

However, Courtois himself has no plans to stop for at least the next five years and sees himself as capable of operating at the highest level for long.

Los Blancos , for their part, will continue assessing the player's performances and rewarding him with optimal renewals based on the same.

As matters stand, however, he is the best goalkeeper in the world and will stay at the club next season. The longer-term plan will depend on his output level.

So far this season, the former Chelsea star has maintained two clean sheets, and the most recent of them came against Villarreal at the weekend.

Needless to say, his objective will be to keep the momentum going as the season progresses into a critical month ahead.

articles.standfirst: El ariete lleva ocho partidos en este ejercicio 2026-27 y no ha anotado, todo lo contrario a las anteriores campañas donde ya se había estrenado en las primeras jornadas
articles.summary: El ariete lleva ocho partidos en este ejercicio 2026-27 y no ha anotado, todo lo contrario a las anteriores campañas donde ya se había estrenado en las primeras jornadas
articles.body: Hugo Duro es el fiel reflejo de lo que está ocurriéndole al Valencia en este inicio de temporada. Ese hundimiento con el que comenzaron el ejercicio ahora toca darle la vuelta a todos y no resulta sencillo. El caso, particularmente, del ariete madrileño es el espejo de una situación global. Duro no ha marcado. Ya son ocho jornadas desde que arrancó la temporada y la sequía es lo más evidente en el delantero de 26 años. La jugada final ante el Racing de Santander demuestra lo que está ocurriendo. En condiciones normales esa jugada que remata Duro es gol pero se va justo por la única rendija que hay fuera del marco. Es el mejor resumen de lo que ha sido hasta ahora. Como el encuentro ante la Real Sociedad antes del parón de tres semanas. En boca de gol faltó un centímetro para que Duro llegara a tocar el esférico en el uno contra uno con Remiro. Es el signo de un inicio de temporada donde no sale nada... y donde no le sale nada al atacante. El caso es que suma 348 minutos en los ocho partidos que ha jugado y no ha visto puerta. No ha jugado tanto con Corberán en el inicio del ejercicio... pero las ocasiones de las que dispuso no se aprovecharon. La mejor prueba para apreciar que el olfato de Duro está en crisis se refrenda con los restantes inicios de temporada y cómo y en qué momento marco el delantero getafense. No necesitó tanto tiempo.

articles.title: El tercer mejor equipo del último mes y medio
articles.standfirst: La Real ha sumado 13 de los 18 últimos puntos, sólo menos que Barcelona y Atlético
articles.summary: La Real ha sumado 13 de los 18 últimos puntos, sólo menos que Barcelona y Atlético
articles.body: La Real Sociedad es el tercer equipo de LaLiga que más puntos ha sumado en las últimas seis jornadas, 13 de 18, sólo por detrás del Barcelona, que ha hecho pleno, y el Atlético de Madrid, que ha logrado 15, lo que deja a las claras lo bien que ha reaccionado el equipo de Pellegrino Matarazzo a las dos derrotas iniciales a domicilio en campos complicadísimos como La Cartuja y el Santiago Bernabéu. La Real, tras tener muchos problemas en la pretemporada por las ausencias de algunos futbolistas internacionales, como el mismísimo Mikel Oyarzabal, y los problemas físicos de otros, como Jon Gorrotxategi, Take Kubo y Pablo Marín, que se pasaron de baja casi toda la preparación, arrancó LaLiga visitando a Betis y Real Madrid, sin sacar puntos, pese a que ante los primeros pudo hacerlo, si llega a tener más puntería. El conjunto txuriurdin compartió el puesto de colista con el Athletic de Bilbao, pero lo abandonó en cuanto venció al Espanyol 2-1, en el estreno de esta campaña en Anoeta. No pudo dar continuidad a ese buen resultado en la siguiente jornada, ante el Celta de nuevo en casa, con una igualada sin dianas, pero después ha conseguido tres victorias en cuatro jornadas, con una derrota por 0-3 frente al Atlético que llegó en los minutos finales y pudo considerarse como un castigo demasiado inmerecido. Los triunfos fueron en Elche y Mestalla, antes del parón, y contra el Deportivo de A Coruña, que estaba siendo uno de los conjuntos revelación, después de los encuentros internacionales. Esos nueve puntos, más los tres logrados antes frente al Espanyol y el sumado con el Celta, suponen 13 en el casillero de una Real que es sexta en la clasificación, un puesto al que no llegaba en solitario desde la última jornada de la temporada 2023-24, hace por tanto más de dos años. En esas seis jornadas en las que los de Matarazzo se han hecho con 13 puntos de los 18 en juego, sólo el Barcelona y el Atlético, con un pleno y 15 puntos, han conseguido más. El Betis ha sumado los mismos, el Real Madrid uno menos y el resto de los rivales de LaLiga ocho o menos. Como apuntamos en MARCA, con Málaha y Levante como contrarios posteriores al Dépor, la escuadra guipuzcoana tiene la oportunidad de situarse en zona europea durante algunas jornadas.
